classes.title: The flat, the week, the family
tags: Class — 30 Aug: the flat, the week, the family
Class — 30 Aug: looking for a flat
classes.covered: A flat room by room and the furniture in it; the seven days of the week; the mother's side of the family and the dual; weather words around ثَلْج; and a reading passage about Samer looking for a flat.

grammar.why: The spine of the whole class — عِنْدِي / عِنْدَكُمْ, and both ways to negate it (مَا عِنْدِي, لَيْسَ عِنْدِي), which she gave together.
Her board question مَاذَا يُوجَدُ فِي بَيْتِكَ مِنَ الأَثَاثِ؟ — the way Arabic says 'there is'.
خَالَانِ وَخَالَتَانِ. Arabic counts one, two, and many; the ـَانِ ending IS the two.
غُرْفَةُ نَوْمٍ, غُرْفَةُ الجُلُوسِ — two nouns pushed together with no word for 'of'. Already on the site; this class is where it earns its keep in everyday speech.
مَا and لَيْسَ, as she used them with عِنْدَ.

notes: أَرَادَ أَنْ + present (أَرَادَ أَنْ يَبْحَثَ — 'he wanted to look for') runs through the passage.
Floors are ordinals: الدَّوْر الثَّالِث, the third floor.
Feminine agreement carries the whole description of the flat: الشَّقَّة جَمِيلَة وَوَاسِعَة.
questions: Did she teach the dual (خَالَانِ / خَالَتَانِ) as a rule, or did it just turn up in a sentence? It changes whether I drill it or only explain it.
The days — did she give them bare (الأَحَد) or with يَوْم in front (يَوْمَ الأَحَدِ)?
Was the passage about Samer read aloud in class, and is reading aloud what she expects next week?
Was the weather set (ثَلْج، مَطَر، سَحَاب) a real topic or an aside off ثَلْج?
What did she set as homework?
